newsitem.title: KENYA: Disease, Zaire crisis hurt Africa coffee, Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Disease, Zaire crisis hurt Africa coffee, Uganda.

text.p: The outbreak of coffee wilt disease in Zaire and heightened civil strife in the Great Lakes region could hit coffee production in Africa despite remarkable gains in recent years.

Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said modest improvements in production in recent years was a result of economic reforms embraced by most African producers such as Uganda and relative political stability in Angola and Rwanda.

"The low yield could meaningfully be overcome with increased farm input and improved crop husbandry, although the outbreak of coffee wilt diasease (tracheomycosis) in Zaire, which has also been sighted in Uganda, could adversely affect the level of output," UCDA said in a report passed to Reuters on Monday.

"However, while there has been appreciable growth in the continent's level of production in recent years, the average yield per hectare (2.471 acres) is at 500 kg (1,102.5 lb), as compared to 1,500 kg (3,307.5 lb) in Latin America and 2,116 kg (4,665.78 lb) in Colombia," UCDA said.
UCDA economists said current political instability in eastern Zaire and Burundi and fighting in southwest Uganda meant that production in the long-term would be adversely affected.
They added that while some stability had returned to Rwanda, it was hoped that a rapid return of thousands of refugees from Zaire would not upset gains made in increasing production.
UCDA said the auction session for Burundi's 1996/97 coffee crop started in August, a month later than normal.

"According to the Office Cafe du Burundi (OCIBU), the delay was attributed to late maturing of the crop, which is forecast to reach 500,000 60-kg bags," UCDA said but did not provide comparative crop figures for 1995/96.
Regional coffee watchers said ethnic strife in Burundi and a regional economic embargo imposed after a July 25 coup that brought Pierre Buyoya to power added to the delay.

UCDA said Africa's coffee output was progressively rising from the 14.7 million 60 kg (132.3 lb) bags in 1993/94 (October-September) to 17 million and 17.1 million bags in 1993/94 and 1994/95 respectively.

"For the 1996/97 season, the continental production is estimated to reach 17.5 million bags. While by the year 2000, it is estimated that production will be in the region of 20 to 22 million bags, a level recorded in 1989/90. This will still be below the record of 30 million bags in the 1960s," UCDA said.
With strife in eastern Zaire, little was being done to combat coffee wilt disease, according to coffee traders.
In Uganda, the UCDA was dealing with the disease by uprooting, chopping and burning affected trees.

In a survey in a key producing district, UCDA said it estimated total coffee lost from a sample of 82.2 acres was about 9,919 kg of clean coffee per year (and equivalent to $9,900 per year) from a total of 18,369 trees.
"The implied economic losses are enormous," UCDA said.
Rivalry between ethnic Hutus and Tutsis, which resulted in nearly one million dead in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, has spilled into Zaire, home to hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees.
Fighting in Zaire pits Zairean troops against Tutsi rebels apparently receiving support from Rwanda. The eastern Zairean towns of Goma and Beni are two major grading centres for Zairean coffee.
